runtime: pre-rendered MP3; offline playback; captions always visible
lines: Somewhere between an ordinary morning and a sky full of stars, a little door waits for curious explorers. Beyond it is the Star House, where every question can become an adventure.
This is Mia. She looks closely, asks what words mean, and makes sure the team never rushes past an important clue.
Sol loves to try things and make his friends laugh. Tavi remembers what the team has already found. Together with Mia, they are the Star House adventure team.
Today, a mysterious note will ask you to find nothing. You will look, listen, move objects and peek behind hiding places. Help the friends say exactly what they find.
Mia, Sol and Tavi stepped into the Star Room. At the far end, the Star Door was closed.
A note slid through the letter box and landed on the floor beside Mia.
Mia saw the note, picked it up and opened it.
A note! It says, ‘Find nothing. Five clues will show the way.’
Find nothing? How do we look for that? Let's follow the clues and find out!
We will look carefully and say what we really find. First, can you spot Mia's note?

You found the note by looking for a sheet of paper with writing on it. Clear names help us tell one object from another. The five empty star shapes will show your progress. The first clue points to the parcel.
The friends followed the arrow across the room. It pointed to a parcel.
I opened the parcel. Look! My brown teddy is inside.
The first clue says to move the teddy. Tap the toy to lift it out. Then tap the box and look inside.

You moved the teddy out and looked inside. The box is empty. Empty means the teddy is not inside the box now. The box is still here. This clue teaches us that empty and nothing do not mean the same thing.
They had found an empty box, not a thing called nothing. The first star turned gold. A blue door opened.
The friends went through the door. They entered a room with three big bells.
Hello! I am Nori. I listen for tiny sounds. May I help you check the bell room?
Yes, please. The note tells us to find nothing. We found an empty box in the first room. Let's check the bells next.
The wind stopped, and the big bell stopped moving. Hold the bell while we stay quiet and listen.
You held the bell still and listened. The bell made no ringing sound, so it was quiet. The bell was still in the room. This clue teaches us that no bell sound is not the same as no bell.
The bell did not ring, but it was still there. The second star turned gold. A door opened to the paper room.
I found a white card on this table. Look, there are no marks on it yet.
Touch the card. You can draw a mark, or choose Leave blank and do not draw.

A card with no mark is called blank. If you drew, the mark appeared on the card. If you left it blank, the card stayed there without a mark. This clue teaches us to say what is missing and what is still present.
The card stayed there with or without a mark. The third star lit. Then seven wall tiles lit up, one after another.
Each glowing tile shows one letter. Read them from left to right with me!
You put seven letters in order to spell nothing. The written word is something we can see and read. This clue teaches us that a word can name an idea without becoming the thing it names.
The written word stayed on the tiles, so the fourth star lit. A gold arrow appeared on the floor and led the friends to a red curtain.
My teddy rolled out of my bag! It crossed the floor and went behind the curtain. I saw where it went, but I cannot see it now!
Slide the curtain slowly. Let's see what is behind it.
There is the teddy. It was hidden: the curtain stopped you from seeing it, but the teddy stayed behind the curtain. This clue teaches us that hidden and gone do not mean the same thing.
Opening the curtain showed the teddy. The fifth star turned gold. Now all five stars were gold, and the Star Door opened.
Behind the Star Door were two small doors, marked A and B. The friends could not see what was behind them yet.
My note still says, Find nothing. Tap both small doors. We must look at each one before we answer.
You checked both doors before answering. One held a card. The other held an empty shelf. Neither showed a thing called nothing. This teaches us to look at all the evidence before we decide.
The friends solved the note's puzzle. Mia folded the note. Everyone carried the five-star map into the library before going home.
Before we put the map away, let's remember the first clue. Which thing became empty after you moved Sol's teddy outside?

You remembered that the box became empty when the teddy moved out. Remembering an earlier clue helps us check what we learned. Mia placed the finished map on the library stand. A hidden ramp opened, and a new parcel slid down beside it. Their next adventure had arrived.

Here is what you learned. We never found a thing called nothing. We found an empty box, a quiet bell, a blank card, the written word nothing and a hidden teddy. Each time, something was still there. This matters because words such as empty, quiet, blank and hidden tell people exactly what you observed.
